service.label: UGC brand finder
service.verb: make short product videos for small brands

first_clients.basis: The first video for each of your first 3 brands at three quarters of your price. At the $100 new-creator price that is $75, the bottom of the $75 to $150 beginner range (Elev8or, checked 2026-10-19).
first_clients.ask: honest feedback, a yes to showing the video in my portfolio once it's live, and a line I may quote, marked as from a founding client

objections.q: We don't have budget for this right now.
objections.a: Understood. The smallest way to try it is one video for one product, with organic use on your own accounts, site and emails.

objections.q: Do you have a portfolio or past work?
objections.a: I'm building my portfolio now, so I'd rather show you than tell you: the concept is made from your own product page, in the style I'd film it.

objections.q: How many followers do you have?
objections.a: UGC goes on your accounts and in your ads, so my follower count doesn't change what you get: the video files and the right to use them, in writing.

objections.q: Would you make it in exchange for free product?
objections.a: I only make paid videos, but I keep the first one small so it's easy to try, and the product you ship is the one I film.

objections.q: Can you promise views or sales?
objections.a: No one honest can promise views or sales: your offer, your ads and the timing decide that. What I promise is what I control: the video on time, one round of edits, and a redo if it misses the brief we agreed on.

objections.q: Can we run it as an ad, and for how long?
objections.a: Yes. Every video comes with organic use: your own accounts, site and emails, for as long as you like. Running it as a paid ad is added per video, for 30 or 90 days from the first day you spend on it.

objections.q: Can you say you've used it for months, or that it fixed something?
objections.a: I only say what I saw and felt after using it, and only once I have. Claims about results need your proof behind them, so they come from you in the brief. That keeps us both inside the FTC's endorsement rules.

objections.q: Can you post it on your own account too?
objections.a: UGC is made for your accounts, but I can post it on mine too. Then it is labeled as an ad: I say "This is an ad for {brand}" in the video and add "#ad Paid partnership with {brand}" to the caption.

call_questions: Which product matters most to you this quarter, and why that one?
Where will the videos run: your product page, your own posts, or paid ads?
How many new videos do you need in a month?
What has worked in your videos so far, and what hasn't?
Who approves the videos, and how fast can they say yes?
What must every video say or never say: claims, words or competitors?
When would you want the first one, and can you ship the product this week?
